key_insight: Random wavefields can form high-probability vortices around island-like holes, with vortex occurrence rising to ~50% in non-rotating cases and nearly 100% when rotation is present.
engineering_relevance: The theory helps predict and control localized vortex formation around obstacles in ocean tides, water-wave devices, and nanophotonic structures.
method: Develop a statistical theory for vortices around islands in 2D random wavefields.
Include and compare cases with and without the Coriolis effect.
Test predicted vortex-charge probabilities against experiments.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimentally validated probability trends versus island size and Coriolis parameter, including strong enhancement for subwavelength islands.
watch_item: The reported vortex statistics depend on island size relative to the characteristic wavelength and on rotational effects, so results may not transfer directly to arbitrary geometries or wave spectra.
paper_title: Vortex formation around islands in random waves
